title: Edge Cases in Hanfu Prompting: When the Rules Do Not Apply
lede: Right lapel over left, one dynasty at a time — these rules work 90% of the time. Here are the 10% where they break, and what to do instead.
body_md:
## Rules are heuristics, not laws
'Right lapel over left' and 'one dynasty at a time' work in most cases. But fashion history is full of exceptions — and a prompt that ignores them produces historically wrong results even while following the rule.

## The 10 percent
**Cross-collar direction**: some ceremonial garments close differently. If your reference shows left-over-right, trust the reference over the rule.
**Dynasty mixing**: Tang fashion genuinely incorporated nomadic (hufu) elements — a Tang+hufu mix is historically valid, not an error.
**Mamian front panel**: modern reinterpretations sometimes pleat the whole skirt. It is still a mamian derivative — do not over-correct.
**Modern fusion**: when writing 'neo-Chinese', historical rules relax; that is the point of the category.

## The meta-rule
Rules exist to produce a recognizable result. When the reference itself is an exception, follow the reference — then state it explicitly in the prompt so the model knows it is intentional.

## Related
Our Hanfu AI Guide and 12-form taxonomy cover the 90% case; this article handles the 10%.
